-   Truong MS., Crone, G., & Choi, JY. (2025) Talk: *Exploring the Multiverse with Decision Trees* Presented at International Meeting of the Psychometric Society 2026. [Slides](pdf/IMPS_mtruong_DTMV_July_16_2026.pdf){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn .btn-page-header .btn-xs role="button"}

    - *Abstract*: There are many decisions to be made in analyzing a dataset, but how do you know which decisions most affect your final results? Both  multiverse analyses and single dataset multi-analyst papers have recently prompted a need for reflecting on the practice of data analysis. These papers can give the impression that you can both ‘follow the rules of statistics’, but also ‘obtain any result you want’. One of the chief concerns is how the combination of the many potential paths that an analyst might traverse can cause the outcome of an analysis to vary the entire spectrum of negative to  positive values, as visualized using a specification curve analysis. Although recent literature has provided guidelines on restricting the number of possible analyses in the multiverse and how to interpret the effects of different paths, there is a gap. Namely, to the best of our knowledge, it is currently difficult for the analyst to select which branch of paths in the multiverse of choices most affected their outcome of interest; and also whether the effect of each path may have been moderated by the paths of other branches. This presentation offers a solution by using R to showcase how the method of decision trees may address this gap, step-by-step. We also discuss cautions for appropriately interpreting the outcome of your decision tree analysis within the context of multiverse analyses.
